_meta.description: Phase 6 of the marketing programme. Three schemas and five seeded standard audiences. The `journey` is authored in pipelinq and COMPILED into an OpenRegister flow (ADR-094); `flowUuid` and `flowStatus` are the only record of that compilation, and pipelinq ships no scheduler of its own. `journeyRun` is the per-contact outcome, and it is what the flow's action node writes so a refusal names the contact it refused. `weeklyReview` holds the numbers pipelinq composed and the narrative an agent may write back, carrying the ADR-088 mark in the same `agentAuthored` / `agentAuthoredBy` pair `article` and `socialPost` already use. The five seeded segments are EXAMPLES a marketer copies: three of them read shillinq signals and resolve to nobody where shillinq is absent, which is the safe direction and is stated in each description.

journey.title: Journey
journey.summary: A trigger, a wait, a condition and one action, compiled into an OpenRegister flow.
journey.description: Authored in pipelinq and executed by OpenRegister's flow engine (ADR-094). Compilation writes flowUuid and flowStatus; nothing here runs until a journey is compiled and active. The action always passes ComplianceService, so a journey can never send where an ordinary blast could not.

name.title: Name
name.description: What this journey is for, in the marketer's own words.
name.example: Win back a customer who has not bought in a year

description.title: Description
description.description: Why the journey exists and who it is meant to reach.

status.title: Status
status.description: A journey only runs while it is active.

audienceSegment.title: Audience
audienceSegment.description: The segment a contact must still match when the action runs. Empty means every contact the trigger delivered.

kind.title: Trigger kind
kind.description: A stage change, a contract renewal window, a list confirmation or a bookkeeping signal.

x-enum-labels.contractRenewalWindow: A contract is up for renewal

cron.title: Schedule
cron.description: Cron expression for a bookkeeping signal, which no object event announces. Ignored by the other three kinds.

waitFor.title: Wait
waitFor.description: How long to wait before the condition is checked, as OpenRegister's wait node reads it. Empty means no wait.

condition.title: Condition
condition.description: One check on the triggering object after the wait. Empty means the action always runs.

field.title: Field
field.description: The field on the triggering object to check.

value.title: Value
value.description: What the field is compared against.

action.title: Action
action.description: What the journey does once the condition holds.

kind.title: Action kind
kind.description: Send a mailing to the contact, or put a task on somebody's list.

templateId.title: Template
templateId.description: The campaign template a mailing is rendered from.

listId.title: Mailing list
listId.description: The list whose consent gate the send is checked against. Empty checks the channel gate instead.

intent.title: Send intent
intent.description: A promotional send is suppressed for a customer in dunning. A service message is not.

taskSubject.title: Task subject
taskSubject.description: The subject of the task a createTask action writes.

taskType.title: Task type
taskType.description: The task type, as the task schema records it.

taskAssignee.title: Task assignee
taskAssignee.description: The user the task goes to. Empty leaves it unassigned.

flowUuid.title: Flow
flowUuid.description: The OpenRegister flow this journey compiled into. Written by the compiler, never by hand.

flowStatus.title: Flow status
flowStatus.description: Whether the flow engine accepted this journey.

flowError.title: Flow error
flowError.description: What the flow engine said, word for word, when it refused. Empty on a clean compile.

createdBy.title: Created by
createdBy.description: The user who wrote this journey.

journeyRun.title: Journey run
journeyRun.summary: What one journey did, or refused to do, for one contact.
journeyRun.description: Written by the pipelinq.journey-action flow node. A refusal is recorded with the contact it refused and the reason, because a journey that quietly skips people looks exactly like a journey with a small audience.

journeyId.title: Journey
journeyId.description: The journey this run belongs to.

contactId.title: Contact
contactId.description: The contact the action was meant for.

clientId.title: Customer
clientId.description: The customer the contact belongs to, when there is one.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why the action was refused or failed. Empty on a send that went out.

actionKind.title: Action kind
actionKind.description: Which action the journey asked for.

flowRunUuid.title: Flow run
flowRunUuid.description: The OpenRegister flow run this step belonged to.

weeklyReview.title: Weekly review
weeklyReview.summary: One page of what moved last week, what to try, and three topic ideas.
weeklyReview.description: Pipelinq composes the numbers from campaigns, social publications and search queries. A hermiq agent may write the narrative back and is then marked as its author (ADR-088). The review takes no action: it has no send and no publish path.

weekStarting.title: Week starting
weekStarting.description: The Monday the reviewed week began on.

sources.title: Sources
sources.description: Which collections the numbers came from.

degraded.title: Missing sources
degraded.description: Collections the review could not read, so a reader knows what is absent rather than assuming it was zero.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: What moved last week, in prose.

highlights.title: Highlights
highlights.description: The few numbers worth reading first.
highlights.example: Webinar AI voor gemeenten reached 120 people

suggestions.title: Suggestions
suggestions.example: Follow up the webinar with a short case study

topicIdeas.title: Topic ideas
topicIdeas.description: Three things worth writing about, drawn from what changed.

agentAuthored.title: Agent authored
agentAuthored.description: Whether an agent wrote the narrative. Applied by the write path itself and ignored when it arrives in a request body, because a mark a client can set is not a mark (ADR-088).

agentAuthoredBy.title: Agent authored by
agentAuthoredBy.description: Identity of the agent that wrote the narrative. Empty on a review nobody added prose to.

blast.description: A blast is one campaign send. A journey that sends a mailing records its deliveries against a blast of its own, so the click redirect, the unsubscribe link and the campaign report keep working on a journey send without a second code path. journeyId is empty on every blast a person composed.

journeyId.title: Journey
journeyId.description: The journey whose sends this blast is the ledger for. Empty on a blast a person composed.

objects.name: Lapsed customers
objects.description: Customers with no invoice for twelve months. Reads shillinq. Where shillinq is absent this audience is empty, which is the safe direction: an unreadable bookkeeping never widens a mailing.

objects.name: Top tier customers
objects.description: Customers whose recognised revenue puts them in the top tier. Reads shillinq, and is empty where shillinq is absent.

objects.name: Advice customers without a product
objects.description: Customers invoiced for the demo advice hour and never for the demo coffee. Copy it and swap the two item names for your own catalogue. Reads shillinq, and is empty where shillinq is absent.

objects.name: Contracts renewing within ninety days
objects.description: Customers whose nearest contract ends in the next ninety days. Reads pipelinq's own contracts, so it resolves on every instance.

objects.name: Leads stalled for thirty days
objects.description: Customers with an open lead that has sat in the same stage for thirty days or more. Reads pipelinq's own leads, so it resolves on every instance.
